articles.description:
A 2FA Backup Code Path Undercut webMethods Integration Server Authentication


IBM published CVE-2026-118904 for webMethods Integration Server 12.1 on 2026-11-03. The bulletin describes improper validation of backup codes during two-factor authentication. A remote attacker who has already authenticated can bypass security restrictions.
The base score is 8.1 with a network vector, low privileges and no user interaction. Confidentiality and integrity impact are high, while availability impact is not listed. The bulletin uses CWE-287, improper authentication, and the vendor provides IS_12.1_Core_Fix1 or later through webMethods Update Manager.
Backup codes exist to keep an administrator from being locked out when a second-factor device is unavailable. That makes them a recovery credential. Re…
articles.title: A 2FA Backup Code Path Undercut webMethods Integration Server Authentication

articles.author: Zero Heartbeat
articles.description:
A method marked [ModuleInitializer] runs before anything else in the assembly — before Main, before the first static field is touched, before any type is used. It is the earliest user code the runtime will run. But the attribute is not what the runtime calls. Open the assembly in a decompiler and the mechanism becomes visible: a static constructor on a type named <Module> that you cannot write by hand, calling your initializer for you.
This is a working deep-dive on that mechanism — what the C# compiler emits for one or several [ModuleInitializer] methods, the metadata that marks the <Module> constructor and separates it from an ordinary type initializer, and how Glass.NET reads it all back into the attributed methods you started with. Glass is a free .NET decompiler, and everything here i…
articles.title: Decompiling module initializers: the <Module> static constructor and ModuleInitializerAttribute

TL;DR: A good toggle switch animation in CSS starts with a real checkbox, so it works with keyboards and screen readers for free. Slide the knob with transform, fade the track colour, and add a short stretch to the knob while it moves. Finish with role="switch", a visible focus ring and a reduced-motion fallback. Or start from the Stretch Toggle in the Capture Motion gallery.
Toggles look simple, but they are one of the most touched controls in any settings screen. A flat jump from left to right works. A knob that leans into the move and settles feels like a physical switch. The extra polish costs about ten lines of CSS.

articles.author: Nana Justine
articles.description:
My Journey So Far as a Freshman SWE at YIBS/ISEST


Starting my journey as a freshman in Software Engineering at YIBS/ISEST has been an exciting and challenging experience. As a new student, I came into this institution with expectations, curiosity, and a strong desire to learn and grow in the field of technology.
My first days at YIBS were filled with excitement and a little nervousness. Meeting new people, getting familiar with the campus, and adjusting to a new academic environment made the experience memorable. Although our class consists of many students, I have gradually started interacting with my classmates and making new acquaintances.
Academically, the journey has been interesting because I have been introduced to several new subjects, including Introduction to Database, Computer Architecture, Operating Systems, Economics, and Programming. Each subject has taught me something different about technology and how computer systems work. Our practical sessions have also given me the opportunity to apply what we learn in class. Learning tools such as VS Code, MySQL, and GitHub has helped me develop my technical skills.
However, the journey has not been without challenges. Some concepts are difficult to understand at first, and adjusting to university-level learning requires discipline, patience, and consistency. Nevertheless, these challenges motivate me to work harder, ask questions, practise regularly, and improve myself.
Beyond academics, YIBS is also helping me develop confidence, communication skills, teamwork, and independence. I am learning that university life is not only about passing examinations but also about building relationships and preparing for the future.
So far, my journey has been a combination of learning, discovery, challenges, and personal growth. Although I still have a long way to go, I am excited about what lies ahead. My goal is to become a skilled and innovative Software Engineer who can use technology to solve real-life problems.
articles.title: My first journey so far as a freshman SWE at YIBS/ISEST.

You've watched the Git tutorial.

I've been there. That's exactly why I built GitMission.

Watching someone run git rebase feels like learning.
It isn't.
Here's what usually happens:
You follow along while the video is playing
You close the tab

Your brain learned to recognize Git. It never learned to use it.

Did you get good by watching, or by doing, failing, and trying again?
Git works the same way. You need to:
